Team —

Quick context: Granite is at legal review and wants to sign by mid-Oct. Their procurement/legal leads have three non-negotiable asks that are gating signature:

1) Per-tenant routing guarantee to US-East with a p95 <= 50ms for synchronous chat at their expected peak (2k RPS). They want routing pinned to region for compliance and low-latency.
2) Weekly export of a customer-scoped audit stream (immutable) delivered to their S3 bucket (encrypted, HSM/KMS-backed). They want schema and delivery SLA defined.
3) A deterministic prompt-redaction step so their PII redaction can be audited end-to-end — they require reproducible redaction outputs for the same inputs for acceptance testing.

We agreed to a pilot. Deal economics are material: $2.1M ARR if we close by Oct 15. Legal has uploaded SOW v2 (attached). They will accept a phased MAP, but product/eng need to confirm feasibility and a reasonable timeline so we can lock the commitment in HubSpot and share with their CTO/Legal.

Ask: can Product/Eng provide a short note with the minimal viable pilot scope and a production path (including if dedicated capacity is required) by EOD Wed? I need to update Tim and legal with a MAP.

Attachments: Granite_SOW_v2.pdf, latency_slo_table.csv

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear ask and the SOW. High-level clarifying questions before we commit timelines:

- Deterministic redaction: do they require bitwise determinism across retries and model version upgrades, or is deterministic output from our redaction module (pre-model) sufficient for their audit tests? In practice model changes break end-to-end reproducibility if we rely on model output for redaction.
- Audit export: what format (JSON L1 events vs. aggregated CSV)? Retention window and whether they want signature on export objects (i.e., manifest + checksum) or a streaming webhook? Also confirm KMS key ownership (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed).
- Routing: is pinning to a single region sufficient or do they expect dedicated physical capacity (reserved pool) to meet the p95 target at 2k RPS?

Proposal for a phased approach:
Option A — Pilot (2 weeks): routing policy + prefix-based cache seeding and weekly S3 export (presigned + manifest). No dedicated capacity. This meets compliance visibility for Timber audit but won't give guaranteed p95 under heavy multi-tenant contention.
Option B — Prod path (6–10 weeks): Dedicated capacity in US-East with tenant-affinity routing, telemetry hooks for per-tenant p95 guarantees, and hardened audit export with signed manifests and retention policies. Option B requires Reserved capacity commit/PO.

If we can get answers to the Qs above, we can lock Option A for pilot with a targeted pilot config by Oct 1 and provide an estimation for Option B next day.

I can run this as the product lead if you want — propose a 30m sync Thu to align MAP and acceptance criteria.

- Laura

Laura/Karthik —

Quick engineering read and constraints:

Routing & latency
- We can implement tenant-scoped routing policies (region pin + affinity) and rate limits via routing layer changes in ~1 full sprint (10 business days) for the pilot config. That will get us a deterministic routing decision and allow them to hit lower observed latency in normal conditions.
- Guaranteeing p95 <= 50ms at 2k RPS requires either Reserved/Dedicated capacity or strict per-tenant throttling and capacity isolation. Multi-tenant shared pools cannot provide that SLA reliably.

Audit export
- We can stream request/response events (metadata + tokens hashed) to S3 daily or weekly. We'll include a signed manifest (SHA256) and per-object encryption metadata. Implementation for a robust export pipeline: ~2–3 weeks to wire and test with a customer bucket and CMK integration.

Deterministic redaction
- Two paths: 1) Pre-model deterministic redaction rules (recommended): deterministic, auditable, and independent of model changes. Implementation: ~1 week to productize ruleset and provide test harness. 2) Model-layer deterministic redaction: much harder; model updates and quantization change outputs and we'd need strict model pinning + test infra to claim determinism — estimate 6+ weeks and would require pinning model versions for the account.

Effort estimate (ballpark): pilot config (Option A) = 2 eng-weeks (routing + export wiring + config); production hardening (Option B) = 6–10 eng-weeks + infra lead time for reserved capacity and billing.

Caveats: any production SLA will require contractual reserved capacity (we cannot promise 50ms p95 on shared tenants). Also need legal sign-off if we store hashed token-level telemetry (PII considerations).

I'll attach the latency SLO table for quick reference.
